chunks: From him, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The traveler continues shortening until he enters his house. So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first report, because his statement, “The traveler continues shortening until he enters his family or his house,” corresponds to what he mentioned in the first report: that when the adhān becomes hidden from him, he shortens. This is by understanding the limit of his entering to his family as the disappearance of the adhān from him. And his statement, “then he enters the houses of Makkah,” may be understood to mean what is near Makkah, even if it is in a place where one there does not hear the adhān, because among the conditions of the adhān is not extreme loudness such that one outside the town at a distance would hear it. In this way, there is no contradiction between the reports.

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the reports or narrations being reconciled
key_terms.الْأَذَانُ: the call to prayer used here as a legal indicator
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرُ: the traveler who is subject to the rulings of travel
key_terms.بَيْتَهُ: his house, marking the endpoint mentioned in the report
key_terms.بُيُوتَ مَكَّةَ: the houses of Makkah, mentioned in explaining proximity to the city
key_terms.غَيْبُوبَةَ: the disappearance or absence of something from perception
key_terms.مُقَصِّرًا: performing qasr, i.e. shortening the prayer

ai.seo_question: Until when may a traveler continue shortening the prayer when returning from سفر?
ai.summary: This text explains a fiqh reconciliation between reports about when a returning traveler stops performing qasr prayer. It clarifies that entering one’s house or family can be understood in relation to the point at which the adhān is no longer heard, thereby removing apparent contradiction between the narrations.
